investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-20T12:32–12:33Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents. Because the failure is upstream of agent creation, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check that calls POST /api/agents received the same 502 bad_gateway response with the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", indicating the failure is in the shared upstream dependency — the swarm ELB or the service behind it — not in any individual check's logic. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 684 minutes old, more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks passed, and there is no evidence of a user-facing outage or shared infrastructure failure.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was last written approximately 684 minutes ago (roughly 11.4 hours), causing the snapshotAgeMinutes assertion in the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json, line 482) to fail. The root cause is a missed or failed workflow execution on the GitHub Actions side, not a problem with the public website itself or the eval runner logic. The exact reason the workflow did not run (scheduling gap, runner failure, permissions issue, or branch protection) cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone.

Second: The workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a step error, authentication failure, or GitHub Pages deployment error) and did not publish a new snapshot, leaving the old file in place.
Third: A GitHub Actions runner availability issue or rate limit caused the workflow to be delayed beyond the 300-minute freshness window.
Fourth: A branch protection rule, permissions change, or secrets rotation prevented the workflow from committing or pushing the updated snapshot to the GitHub Pages branch.
